text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2212345678 — kv-cache eviction storm + continuous-batching surge detected in prod-west1. Severity: P1. Pager: @micah. Auto-runbook: <https://internal/runbooks/kv-eviction-storm|kv-eviction-storm>.

micah: on it. paging now. seeing huge eviction/sec on kv-* shards. pct cache usage dropped from ~82% -> 18% in ~3m. traffic spike?

jordana: grabbing metrics — query-ing ops metrics. can you post the last deploy id for kv-serving? suspect a batch config pushed earlier.

micah: last deploy: sha: a1b2c3d4 (kv-batching-tweak). rolled 10:12 UTC. spike started ~10:16. linking perf graphs: <https://dash/g/kv/evictions?from=10:00&to=10:30>.

sree: preliminary triage: continuous batching appears to coalesce many small requests into huge GPU batches causing KV read amplification + heavy KV cache churn. eviction TTLs can't keep up -> fragmentation. recommendation: throttle batching and enable eviction backpressure immediately.

micah: ok executing emergency config patch to throttle batching and enable eviction throttle. patching via redwoodctl. will post command and output.

micah: ```
# emergency: reduce continuous batching concurrency + enable eviction throttle
redwoodctl config set service/kv-serving kv.batch.max_concurrent_requests=24
redwoodctl config set service/kv-serving kv.cache.eviction_throttle=1
redwoodctl rollout restart deployment/kv-serving --namespace=prod-west1
```

deploy-bot: rollout starting for deployment/kv-serving (namespace=prod-west1) — rollout id: r-9987. rolling update across 8 pods. ETA ~4m.

jason: while that rolls, note that allocator fragmentation metrics (cuda_malloc_total / arena_free_ratio) are spiking. if evictions keep happening, pytorch caching allocator is starving large contiguous allocations -> OOM risk. plan: schedule arena compaction and a targeted process restart for highest-frag pods.

micah: rollout completed — 8/8 pods up. eviction/sec dropping. graph: eviction/sec pre: 3.2k -> post: 680 (approx 79% drop). latency P95 improved from 220ms -> 95ms.

sree: nice. still seeing residual fragmentation on 2 pods (kv-5, kv-7). suggest run arena compaction on those first to avoid cuda malloc failures. command below.

jason: ```
# run arena compaction on selected pods
kubectl exec -n prod-west1 pod/kv-5 -- python /opt/tools/arena_compact.py --pool kv_cache --aggressive
kubectl exec -n prod-west1 pod/kv-7 -- python /opt/tools/arena_compact.py --pool kv_cache --aggressive
# also toggle torch caching split size to reduce fragmentation risk
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=\"max_split_size_mb:128\"
```

ops-bot: arena_compact job queued on kv-5, kv-7. job ids: jc-421, jc-422.

micah: running compaction now. will monitor cuda malloc stderr on those pods. attaching recent stderr tail from kv-5: ```
[WARN] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory at step 14321
[INFO] arena free ratio: 0.03, total_frag_bytes: 2.1GB
```

support-bot: notice: a small set of customers experienced 502s between 10:15-10:22 UTC. support alert created: INC-9082. affected: cust-alfred, cust-zenai. priority: medium for customer communication.

jordana: putting customer impact note in the runbook. we should proactively message top affected accounts. micah, can you confirm duration and whether retries succeeded?

micah: window ~7m, retry success rate ~96% (some requests hit eviction storm and retried). I'll hand payload to support with logs.

sree: compaction finished on kv-5 and kv-7. post-compaction metrics: arena_free_ratio -> 0.34, total_frag_bytes down to 320MB. no further cudaMalloc errors observed on stderr.

jason: re: root cause hypothesis — the batching change increased max batch size and removed a soft cap on per-model prefix coalescing. small prefixes got merged into large batches that (1) forced many KV lookups per large token window and (2) created hot reallocation patterns in the allocator. combined effect -> cache churn + fragmentation.

micah: action items so far:
- rolled back continuous-batching max increase (emergency config).
- enabled eviction_throttle.
- targeted arena compaction executed on 2 pods.
- set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF on rollout image for next patch.
- created support incident INC-9082 and notified customers.

jason: we should also schedule a canary for the rollback in prod-east to ensure no regression on throughput. propose canary window 30m with stricter batching caps.

deploy-bot: deploy r-9988 (rollback of a1b2c3d4) queued for prod-east canary. will deploy to 2 pods first.

micah: handing off to jordana for the 2hr follow-up and investigation / postmortem. I need to sleep. tagging @jordana +oncall.

jordana: taking handoff. will run full heap/profile capture for kv-serving during the incident window and start a P0 Jira for allocator/continuous-batching changes. timeline to follow in the runbook.

support-bot: note posted to affected customers: "We observed a transient degradation in inference throughput between 10:15–10:22 UTC which impacted request latencies and caused intermittent errors for some customers. Our mitigation is in place and service stabilized. Follow-up email will be sent with root-cause and actions." :thumbsup:

micah: thanks team. leaving marker in runbook with commands used and metric snapshots. handing off full logs to jordana: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2212345678/

jordana: will own postmortem. initial severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 after stabilization and no lingering customer impact. created PM ticket: RD-INC-2212345678.

ops-bot: reminder: please attach dotfiles/profile dumps to the ticket and label with `kv-eviction-storm` `allocator` `continuous-batching`.

micah: :wave: handoff complete. good catch on the batching change. follow-up items captured.

jason: quick note for next steps: add a circuit-breaker on batch assembly size and introduce a health-check that fails fast if eviction/sec > threshold for >30s. also add an automated compaction trigger when arena_free_ratio < 0.1.

jordana: added to backlog and prioritized. closing incident thread, will update PM and postmortem when draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
